messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Times in the app are rendered by the server, in the server's timezone. That's
wrong for anyone anywhere else, and it kills page caching: everyone's clock
ends up baked into HTML we'd like to share between people.

Move time rendering into the browser, everywhere we show a date or time. The
server sends the raw timestamp; the page turns it into words in the viewer's
own timezone. A comment from two hours ago reads "1:42 PM"; one from last
night reads "yesterday"; one from earlier in the week reads "5 days ago" or
"Sep 12"; a card auto-closing overnight reads "tomorrow", further out "in 3
days".


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
--- STYLE.md ---

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

Okay, so the problem is clear: the server's timezone is baking times into the HTML, killing page caching and giving everyone the wrong time. The solution is to move the time rendering to the browser, sending raw timestamps from the server and having the client transform them into the user's local timezone and present human-readable time strings. "A comment from two hours ago reads '1:42 PM'; one from last night reads 'yesterday'; one from earlier in the week reads '5 days ago' or 'Sep 12'; a card auto-closing overnight reads 'tomorrow', further out 'in 3 days'." Got it. Server sends raw, client renders relative/local.

Now, let's dissect the codebase. I'm going to meticulously examine every file related to time, dates, and timezones. I need to understand where the current time logic lies, and how it is being used, so that I can figure out the best way to extract it.   include Serializable

  attr_reader :user, :day, :filter

  delegate :today?, to: :day

  def initialize(user, day, filter)
    @user, @day, @filter = user, day, filter
  end

  def has_activity?
    events.any?
  end

  def events
    filtered_events.where(created_at: window).order(created_at: :desc)
  end

  def next_day
    latest_event_before&.created_at
  end

  def earliest_time
    next_day&.tomorrow&.beginning_of_day
  end

  def latest_time
    day.yesterday.beginning_of_day
  end

  def added_column
    @added_column ||= build_column(:added, "Added", 1, events.where(action: %w[card_published card_reopened]))
  end

  def updated_column
    @updated_column ||= build_column(:updated, "Updated", 2, events.where.not(action: %w[card_published card_closed card_reopened]))
  end

  def closed_column
    @closed_column ||= build_column(:closed, "Done", 3, events.where(action: "card_closed"))
  end

  def cache_key
    ActiveSupport::Cache.expand_cache_key [ user, filter, day.to_date, Time.zone.name, events ], "day-timeline"
  end

  private
    TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS = %w[
      card_assigned
      card_unassigned
      card_published
      card_closed
      card_reopened
      card_collection_changed
      card_board_changed
      card_postponed
      card_auto_postponed
      card_triaged
      card_sent_back_to_triage
      comment_created
    ]

    def filtered_events
      @filtered_events ||= begin
        events = timelineable_events
        events = events.where(creator_id: filter.creators.ids) if filter.creators.present?
        events
      end
    end

    def timelineable_events
      Event
        .preloaded
        .where(board: boards)

class User::DayTimeline
  include Serializable

  attr_reader :user, :day, :filter

  delegate :today?, to: :day

  def initialize(user, day, filter)
    @user, @day, @filter = user, day, filter
  end

  def has_activity?
    events.any?
  end

  def events
    filtered_events.where(created_at: window).order(created_at: :desc)
  end

  def next_day
    latest_event_before&.created_at
  end

  def earliest_time
    next_day&.tomorrow&.beginning_of_day
  end

  def latest_time
    day.yesterday.beginning_of_day
  end

  def added_column
    @added_column ||= build_column(:added, "Added", 1, events.where(action: %w[card_published card_reopened]))
  end

  def updated_column
    @updated_column ||= build_column(:updated, "Updated", 2, events.where.not(action: %w[card_published card_closed card_reopened]))
  end

  def closed_column
    @closed_column ||= build_column(:closed, "Done", 3, events.where(action: "card_closed"))
  end

  def cache_key
    ActiveSupport::Cache.expand_cache_key [ user, filter, day.to_date, Time.zone.name, events ], "day-timeline"
  end

  private
    TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS = %w[
      card_assigned
      card_unassigned
      card_published
      card_closed
      card_reopened
      card_collection_changed
      card_board_changed
      card_postponed
      card_auto_postponed
      card_triaged
      card_sent_back_to_triage
      comment_created
    ]

    def filtered_events
      @filtered_events ||= begin
        events = timelineable_events
        events = events.where(creator_id: filter.creators.ids) if filter.creators.present?
        events
      end
    end

    def timelineable_events
      Event
        .preloaded
        .where(board: boards)
        .where(action: TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS)
    end

    def boards
      filter.boards.presence || user.boards
    end

    def latest_event_before
      filtered_events.where(created_at: ...day.beginning_of_day).chronologically.last
    end

    def build_column(id, base_title, index, events)
      Column.new(self, id, base_title, index, events)
    end

    def window
      day.all_day
    end
end

=== notifications_helper.rb ===
module NotificationsHelper
  def event_notification_title(event)
    case event_notification_action(event)
    when "comment_created" then "RE: #{card_notification_title(event.eventable.card)}"
    else card_notification_title(event.eventable)
    end
  end

  def event_notification_body(event)
    creator = event.creator.name

    case event_notification_action(event)
    when "card_assigned" then "Assigned to #{event.assignees.none? ? "self" : event.assignees.pluck(:name).to_sentence}"
    when "card_unassigned" then "Unassigned by #{creator}"
    when "card_published" then "Added by #{creator}"
    when "card_closed" then "Moved to Done by #{creator}"
    when "card_reopened" then "Reopened by #{creator}"
    when "card_postponed" then "Moved to Not Now by #{creator}"
    when "card_auto_postponed" then "Moved to Not Now due to inactivity"
    when "card_title_changed" then "Renamed by #{creator}"
    when "card_board_changed" then "Moved by #{creator}"
    when "card_triaged" then "Moved to #{event.particulars.dig("particulars", "column")} by #{creator}"
    when "card_sent_back_to_triage" then "Moved back to Maybe? by #{creator}"
    when "comment_created" then comment_notification_body(event)
    else creator
    end
  end

  def notification_tag(notification, &)
    tag.div id: dom_id(notification), class: "tray__item tray__item--notification", data: {
      navigable_list_target: "item",
      card_id: notification.card.id
    } do
      link_to(notification,
        class: [ "card card--notification", { "card--closed": notification.card.closed? }, { "unread": !notification.read? } ],
        data: { turbo_frame: "_top", badge_target: "unread", action: "badge#update dialog#close" },
        style: { "--card-color:": notification.card.color },
        &)
    end
  end

  def notification_toggle_read_button(notification, url:)
    if notification.read?
      button_to url,
          method: :delete,
          class: "card__notification-unread-indicator btn btn--circle borderless",
          title: "Mark as unread",
          data: { action: "form#submit:stop badge#update:stop", form_target: "submit" },
          form: { data: { controller: "form" } } do
        concat(icon_tag("unseen"))
      end
    else
      button_to url,
          class: "card__notification-unread-indicator btn btn--circle borderless",
          title: "Mark as read",
          data: { action: "form#submit:stop badge#update:stop", form_target: "submit" },
          form: { data: { controller: "form" } } do
        concat(icon_tag("remove"))
        concat(tag.span(notification.unread_count, class: "badge-count")) if notification.unread_count > 1
      end
    end
  end

  def notifications_next_page_link(page)
    unless @page.last?
      tag.div id: "next_page", data: { controller: "fetch-on-visible", fetch_on_visible_url_value: notifications_path(page: @page.next_param) }
    end
  end

  def bundle_email_frequency_options_for(settings)
    options_for_select([
      [ "Never", "never" ],
      [ "Every few hours", "every_few_hours" ],
      [ "Every day", "daily" ],
      [ "Every week", "weekly" ]
    ], settings.bundle_email_frequency)
  end

  private
    def event_notification_action(event)
      if event.action.card_published? && event.eventable.assigned_to?(event.creator)
        "card_assigned"
      else
        event.action
      end
    end

    def comment_notification_body(event)
      comment = event.eventable
      comment.body.to_plain_text.truncate(200)
    end

    def card_notification_title(card)
      card.title.presence || "Card #{card.number}"
    end

module NotificationsHelper
  def event_notification_title(event)
    case event_notification_action(event)
    when "comment_created" then "RE: #{card_notification_title(event.eventable.card)}"
    else card_notification_title(event.eventable)
    end
  end

  def event_notification_body(event)
    creator = event.creator.name

    case event_notification_action(event)
    when "card_assigned" then "Assigned to #{event.assignees.none? ? "self" : event.assignees.pluck(:name).to_sentence}"
    when "card_unassigned" then "Unassigned by #{creator}"
    when "card_published" then "Added by #{creator}"
    when "card_closed" then "Moved to Done by #{creator}"
    when "card_reopened" then "Reopened by #{creator}"
    when "card_postponed" then "Moved to Not Now by #{creator}"
    when "card_auto_postponed" then "Moved to Not Now due to inactivity"
    when "card_title_changed" then "Renamed by #{creator}"
    when "card_board_changed" then "Moved by #{creator}"
    when "card_triaged" then "Moved to #{event.particulars.dig("particulars", "column")} by #{creator}"
    when "card_sent_back_to_triage" then "Moved back to Maybe? by #{creator}"
    when "comment_created" then comment_notification_body(event)
    else creator
    end
  end

  def notification_tag(notification, &)
    tag.div id: dom_id(notification), class: "tray__item tray__item--notification", data: {
      navigable_list_target: "item",
      card_id: notification.card.id
    } do
      link_to(notification,
        class: [ "card card--notification", { "card--closed": notification.card.closed? }, { "unread": !notification.read? } ],
        data: { turbo_frame: "_top", badge_target: "unread", action: "badge#update dialog#close" },
        style: { "--card-color:": notification.card.color },
        &)
    end
  end

  def notification_toggle_read_button(notification, url:)
    if notification.read?
      button_to url,
          method: :delete,
          class: "card__notification-unread-indicator btn btn--circle borderless",
          title: "Mark as unread",
          data: { action: "form#submit:stop badge#update:stop", form_target: "submit" },
          form: { data: { controller: "form" } } do
        concat(icon_tag("unseen"))
      end
    else
      button_to url,
          class: "card__notification-unread-indicator btn btn--circle borderless",
          title: "Mark as read",
          data: { action: "form#submit:stop badge#update:stop", form_target: "submit" },
          form: { data: { controller: "form" } } do
        concat(icon_tag("remove"))
        concat(tag.span(notification.unread_count, class: "badge-count")) if notification.unread_count > 1
      end
    end
  end

  def notifications_next_page_link(page)
    unless @page.last?
      tag.div id: "next_page", data: { controller: "fetch-on-visible", fetch_on_visible_url_value: notifications_path(page: @page.next_param) }
    end
  end

  def bundle_email_frequency_options_for(settings)
    options_for_select([
      [ "Never", "never" ],
      [ "Every few hours", "every_few_hours" ],
      [ "Every day", "daily" ],
      [ "Every week", "weekly" ]
    ], settings.bundle_email_frequency)
  end

  private
    def event_notification_action(event)
      if event.action.card_published? && event.eventable.assigned_to?(event.creator)
        "card_assigned"
      else
        event.action
      end
    end

    def comment_notification_body(event)
      comment = event.eventable
      comment.body.to_plain_text.truncate(200)
    end

    def card_notification_title(card)
      card.title.presence || "Card #{card.number}"
    end
end

export default class extends BridgeComponent {
  static component = "stamp"
  static values = { scopeSelector: { type: String, default: "body" } }

  connect() {
    super.connect()

    if (this.element.closest(this.scopeSelectorValue)) {
      this.notifyBridgeOfConnect()
      this.#observeStamp()
    }
  }

  disconnect() {
    super.disconnect()
    this.notifyBridgeOfDisconnect()
    this.stampObserver?.disconnect()
  }

  notifyBridgeOfConnect() {
    const bridgeElement = this.bridgeElement

    this.send("connect", {
      title: bridgeElement.title,
      description: bridgeElement.bridgeAttribute("description")
    })
  }

  notifyBridgeOfDisconnect() {
    this.send("disconnect")
  }

  #observeStamp() {
    this.stampObserver = new MutationObserver(() => {
      this.notifyBridgeOfConnect()
    })

    this.stampObserver.observe(this.element, {
      attributes: true
    })
  }
}

**Deep Dive into Timezone Rendering and Caching**

Alright, let's break this down. The core issue is server-side time rendering and its impact on caching, as I understand it. Right now, the server dictates the time, and that's problematic. It locks us into a specific timezone, which breaks down the page's ability to be properly and efficiently cached. Every user gets a version of the page specific to their own timezone. That's inefficient and misses the benefits of sharing resources.

The goal is clear: move all date and time formatting to the browser. The server only sends the raw timestamp, and the client-side JavaScript, using the user's timezone, will take over the formatting. This includes relative times ("2 hours ago", "yesterday", "tomorrow") and absolute dates ("Sep 12").

The implications of the move are quite complex, especially considering existing time-related code. From my detailed inspection, I'm focusing on the `cards` (`_meta.html.erb` partials, the styles in `cards.css`, etc.) and especially `app/views/cards/container/_closure.html.erb`, which is very relevant to this issue. The format strings should be adjusted to be more specific (e.g. "Added 1:42 PM" vs "Added 5 days ago"). The crucial thing is that date/time rendering has to be flexible to accommodate different contexts.

A careful review of all date and time usage throughout the app is necessary! I'm listing all the views and helper methods to ensure nothing is missed (e.g., in `cards/_comment.html.erb`, `events/day_timeline`, `webhooks/_delivery`, and various others, including all the `bridge_helper` methods). The goal is to move those server-rendered date/time formats, which are currently being rendered with formats like `%A, %B %-d` or `%l:%M %p`, to client-side rendering.

The `CurrentTimezone` concern is interesting. I understand it and how cookies work to render for a user's local timezone. And now I see that the caching has to vary by timezone, or it will be wrong for certain users. And the timezone cookie also gets embedded into the `etag`, which also splits the cache!

What about the impact on `DayTimeline` and `Events`?
The `DayTimeline` uses `Time.zone.parse` on the server! Is that part of what's broken? Or should that stay and just switch to client-side?
That part needs careful consideration because the hourly grid calculations and cache keys depend on the server timezone settings. I'm going to carefully read `date_helpers.js`, `bubble_controller.js` and `timezone_cookie_controller.js`, and how `day_timeline` is rendered in `events.css`.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Time Rendering in the Application**

Okay, let's break this down. My goal is to move all time rendering to the browser. Right now, the server handles it, causing problems with page caching because everyone sees times in the server's timezone, which is bad for shared data and caching. We need to send the raw timestamps and let the browser handle formatting for the viewer's timezone.

First, I examined how `events` work. I see that `EventsController` uses `CurrentTimezone`, setting `Time.zone` based on a cookie. This is important because `day = Time.current` or `Time.zone.parse(params[:day])` uses the user's timezone to compute `day.all_day` and how events are grouped by hour with `grid-area`. I see two tests using specific timezones, which is a good sign, and one tests ensuring the timezone cookie is in the ETag.

Then I checked out the templates:
-   `app/models/user/day_timeline/column.rb` renders dates using `strftime`.
-   `app/views/events/day_timeline/_column.html.erb` renders timestamps using `strftime`.
-   `app/views/events/_empty_days.html.erb` renders dates with `strftime`.
-   `app/views/events/day_timeline/_columns.html.erb` caches based on `Time.zone.name`.

All these templates are where the current time rendering is happening, and it's all server-side with `Time.zone`. Also, the `Current.user` has its timezone stored and is used for email notifications! And the `date_helpers.js` has a `<meta name="timezone">` tag!

I saw clues that point to what I need to do: the existing code uses `date_helpers.js` and there are existing rules and conventions in the stylesheets about using `.local-time-value` in the HTML, and the `TimeHelper` is ALREADY included in `User::DayTimeline::Column`. So, it looks like there were previous efforts here. It looks like the team knew that they needed a `TimeHelper` and a local-time controller.

The clue is clear: "Move time rendering into the browser, everywhere we show a date or time. The server sends the raw timestamp; the page turns it into words in the viewer's own timezone." The current caching strategy is a mess. Dates and times are baked into cached HTML, and everyone sees the server's timezone.

We need to make this change by:
1.  Identifying all places where dates and times are rendered by the server. I found many of them!
2.  Switching those to render the raw timestamp instead.
3.  Implement a client-side solution that converts the raw timestamp into words in the viewer's timezone.

messages.thinking:
**Comprehensive Timezone and Time Formatting Analysis**

Okay, let's break this down. First, the codebase is remarkably clean, which is a great starting point. We need to audit all time-related code to ensure consistency across the application. My initial thoughts revolve around how `time_helper.rb` and `local-time` integrate, specifically considering Turbo morphing and the roles of `turbo-rails`, `turbo:morph`, `connect()`, `disconnect()`, and MutationObservers (or Stimulus controllers).

**Design Question 1: Timezone Management Strategy**

The core issue is that times are currently rendered on the server, in the server's timezone, which breaks caching and provides incorrect times to users in different zones. The objective is to move rendering to the browser.

*   `app/javascript/helpers/date_helpers.js`: Initially, this file used a `timezone` meta tag for snapping timestamps to midnight, ensuring client-side date boundaries match the server's. However, this meta tag approach causes a problem for the initial page load for a user, as the initial value of this tag is likely to be UTC. Thus, for that initial page load, times will appear in UTC instead of the user's local timezone.

*   `app/views/layouts/shared/_head.html.erb`: The meta tag `name="timezone"` is populated with `Time.zone.name`. This would also cause problems with caching.

*   `app/controllers/concerns/current_timezone.rb`: This uses an `around_action` to set `Time.zone` based on the `timezone` cookie and also includes an `etag` that includes this timezone. This would cause issues with caching if the timezone changed, as the cached version would be specific to each user, but if we don't include the timezone in the cache key or the etag, it breaks important test cases.

**Key Insight:** Instead of using the `meta` tag or `Time.zone`, we should leverage the **viewer's browser timezone** directly via `Intl.DateTimeFormat()` when rendering the timestamps in the browser. **Timezone Transformation: A Deep Dive into Date and Time Rendering**

Okay, so I've been digging into this time zone issue, and it's become clear that we need to make some fundamental changes to how we render dates and times. The goal, as I understand it, is to move time rendering into the browser, ensuring that users see times in *their* time zone, not the server's. This has massive implications for caching, because the current approach "bakes" the server's time into the HTML, which is bad.

Initially, I was focused on how we cache fragments like comments, notifications, and card previews, where previously the date formatting in the views was done server-side. I've switched to using `local_datetime_tag` to render the timestamp directly, eliminating the timezone information that can cause cache invalidation.

However, the real puzzle was the `day_timeline` and its connection to the `events` view. The code here is more complex and has given me a little bit of trouble. I've realized that the problem lies in the way we handle the `day` parameter and the interaction with the `cookies[:timezone]` cookie. Initially, the server was doing the time zone conversion, causing the date to be interpreted incorrectly in the browser.

Specifically, I’ve found that `day_timeline.day` is parsed from the URL `params[:day]`, but this can be a date-only string like "2025-01-20". When the cookie isn't set, `Time.zone` is assumed to be UTC, which causes a "day shift" when interpreted in a browser's local timezone.

After some analysis, I've realized the best solution is to ensure `earliest`, `latest`, and `day_timeline.day` are all passed as `Time` objects. Then, when a user's `cookies[:timezone]` is set, the browser knows to render the time correctly. And if the timezone cookie isn't set, then the browser shows the correct timestamp anyway because the javascript will use UTC as the default and still render the correct date/time.

The key to all this is that, when rendering `Date` objects, using `datetime.iso8601` with `local_datetime_tag` prevents any UTC-midnight day shifts.

Now, with this understanding, I can be certain the page will always display the correct date, and the cache will work. I've gone over the code for the `events` timeline to make sure this is consistent, including the `_empty_days.html.erb` partial, where `earliest` and `latest` (now `Time` objects and *not* `Date` objects) are displayed. By using these date/time conversions and passing them directly to the `local_datetime_tag`, we've solved the timezone display and caching problem across the entire application.

I'm confident that this approach guarantees that the time shown will always match what is on the screen, across all timezones.

If a user with a specific timezone cookie accesses a public page, the CDN will cache *that* timezone, potentially serving incorrect timezone information to other users.

The `CurrentTimezone` concern is interesting. It looks like `EventsController`, `Events::DaysController`, and related controllers use `Time.zone` extensively for the `DayTimeline` feature. The `_time_zone.html.erb` partial is syncing `Current.user.timezone` using `timezone_from_cookie`, and this is all managed by `CurrentTimezone`. Critically, there are tests that rely on the `etag { timezone_from_cookie }` logic, meaning we need to be very careful when changing this behavior. These tests are the ones in `current_timezone_test.rb` and `events_controller_test.rb`.

My strategy here is to leverage the browser's native timezone. The plan is to have `date_helpers.js` *not* rely on the `<meta name="timezone">` tag, and instead use the browser's local timezone. This is important to ensure that even with public caching, offline PWAs, or when a cached page has a stale timezone meta tag, the browser will always render times correctly for the viewer's current location.

Let's test the `signedDifferenceInDays` function in `date_helpers.js`. If we have a date "2025-01-22 23:30:00" in the viewer's local timezone (UTC-5), and another date "2025-01-23 00:30:00" in the viewer's local timezone, it should return +1. The `beginningOfDay` function is the key and uses `Date.UTC`, which ensures that days are always calculated correctly, regardless of DST transitions. We just need to make sure to account for how JavaScript handles parsing date strings with and without time components. A date-only string like "2025-01-22" is interpreted as UTC, which can lead to off-by-one errors if we aren't careful. If passing a date, we parse as a local time, if passing an ISO8601 string, we parse as an instant.

Sending only the date part via `day_timeline.day.to_date` is the right move, since the helper is always generating the *calendar* date.

What about timestamps with time components? For example, in `_column.html.erb`, `events.first.created_at` is a timestamp, and we should show the time in the viewer's timezone. By using the browser timezone, the date and time will be displayed in the correct local time, regardless of what's cached.

class CardRefreshTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
    @card = cards(:layout)
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes made elsewhere" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "h1", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh preserves an edit in progress" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title

    within_edit_frame do
      fill_in_lexxy with: "Draft description in progress"
    end

    update_card_elsewhere

    # The title change's system comment appearing proves the refresh reached the page.
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5
    within_edit_frame do
      assert_selector "lexxy-editor", text: "Draft description in progress"
    end
    assert_no_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "canceling an edit reveals card changes made elsewhere during the edit" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    update_card_elsewhere
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5

    send_keys :escape

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere"
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes after an edit is canceled" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    send_keys :escape
    assert_selector "a.card__title-link", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  private
    def update_card_elsewhere
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      @card.update!(title: "Retitled elsewhere", description: "Description updated elsewhere")
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob
    end

    # A broadcast sent before the page's subscriptions are confirmed is lost.
    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end

    def within_edit_frame(&block)
      within "##{dom_id(@card, :edit)}", &block
    end
end

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  private
    def update_card_elsewhere
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      @card.update!(title: "Retitled elsewhere", description: "Description updated elsewhere")
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob
    end

    # A broadcast sent before the page's subscriptions are confirmed is lost.
    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end

    def within_edit_frame(&block)
      within "##{dom_id(@card, :edit)}", &block
    end
end

**Analyzing Turbo Morph and Local Time Updates**

Okay, let's break down how this works. I'm looking at `CardRefreshTest`, and I see that when a card updates and broadcasts a Turbo morph refresh, `local-time` elements on the card are going to get their `datetime` attributes updated, thanks to `turbo:morph-element`. That's the key.

Now, if a `local_datetime_tag` has `turbo:morph-element->local-time#refresh:self`, or uses `data-local-time-datetime-value` or a `MutationObserver`, here's what happens during a Turbo Morph (using Idiomorph, specifically):

Imagine a `<time>` element in the DOM like this: `<time datetime="2025-01-22T17:30:00Z" ...>12:30 PM</time>`. If `card.last_active_at` changes to, say, `2025-01-22T18:00:00Z`, a morph occurs. The server sends back updated HTML: `<time datetime="2025-01-22T18:00:00Z" ... data-action="turbo:morph-element->local-time#refresh:self"></time>`.

Here's the critical sequence:

1.  Idiomorph updates the `datetime` attribute, *removes `title`*, and *clears the innerText* to an empty string (""). That's important!
2.  Idiomorph then dispatches `turbo:morph-element` on the `<time>` element.
3.  The `data-action` attribute, `turbo:morph-element->local-time#refresh:self`, immediately triggers the `refresh()` method on the `local-time` controller. This re-renders the time, including the string and `title`.
4.  And here's where it gets interesting: Even if the `datetime` attribute *didn't* change during a morph (say, the card title changes, re-rendering the card but keeping the same `created_at` date), Idiomorph *still* clears the `<time>` element's innerText! Now, if we *only* relied on `datetimeValueChanged`, the time wouldn't re-render if the `datetime` attribute stayed the same.

That's a potentially huge bug, and I need to verify that!

During the Turbo morph, the server sends `<time ...></time>` (empty innerText). Idiomorph morphs something like `<time>1:42 PM</time>` into `<time></time>`, wiping the time display. Since `data-controller="local-time"` was already connected, Stimulus *doesn't* call `connect()` again. And because the `datetime` didn't change, `datetimeValueChanged()` *wouldn't* fire!

But `turbo:morph-element` *is* dispatched by Turbo/Idiomorph on every morphed element, and if the app is handling `turbo:morph@window->local-time#refresh` or `data-action="turbo:morph-element->local-time#refresh:self"` in the `local_time_controller.js`, it IMMEDIATELY updates `<time>` after the morph!

Now I'm thinking about parent elements being morphed and impacting the `<time>` element, so I'll check how `turbo:morph-element` is handled in `@hotwired/turbo-rails`, potentially by examining `morph_guard_controller.js` or `multi_selection_combobox_controller.js` to see how those apps handle morphing.

**My Thoughts on Timezone Refactoring**

Wow, that `grep` result is fantastic! Every date and time displayed in the browser's HTML across the codebase now utilizes `local_datetime_tag`, except for those pesky pagination URL parameters and that fixed `MagicLink::EXPIRATION_TIME` duration. Okay, let's move on to the real work – writing comprehensive tests!

First, I'll focus on unit/helper tests for `TimeHelper` in `test/helpers/time_helper_test.rb`. That should cover the low-level logic. Then, the system tests are where the rubber meets the road. I'll need to verify the browser rendering behaves as expected. Here's a quick checklist of the critical scenarios:

*   A comment posted a couple of hours ago should render as, say, "1:42 PM" as seen in the viewer's timezone.
*   A comment posted last night needs to show "yesterday," even if it’s technically less than 24 hours ago.
*   Comments from 5 days ago should render as "5 days ago," and anything older than 7 days should show "Sep 12" or "Sep 12, 2024" if from a prior year.
*   A card closing overnight must display "tomorrow," and another card, closing further out, needs to render as "in 3 days," as appropriate.
*   Crucially, I need to validate that viewer timezone rendering works accurately, even when the viewer's timezone differs from UTC. `TZ` and browser timezone settings are going to be key.
*   Caching is another essential aspect to test. Rendering the same cached card/comment HTML across users in different timezones needs to produce identical HTML with raw UTC timestamps. Then, confirm the browser correctly renders the timestamps according to the viewer's timezone.
*   I can't forget Turbo morphing - the `CardRefreshTest` and updating card scenario must retain the proper `<time>` rendering.
*   Finally, I need to confirm that `bubble_controller.js` and `date_helpers.js` function correctly without relying on the `meta[name="timezone"]` tag.

Before diving deep into writing new tests, I'll run the existing controller and system tests to make sure that these massive changes didn't break anything. It's best to confirm the base is stable before introducing brand new scenarios.

**Testing Timezone Rendering: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm thinking about how to effectively test timezone rendering, specifically in `test/system/local_time_test.rb`. I've got two main approaches in mind using headless Chrome (Selenium): utilizing `execute_cdp` or setting the `Date` on the server. The `execute_cdp` method, specifically `Emulation.setTimezoneOverride`, seems promising because it directly alters the browser's timezone, overriding `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, the browser's `Date#getHours()`, and `Date#getTimezoneOffset()`! Alternatively, I could set the `Date` or use `travel_to` on the server, but `travel_to` only affects the Ruby server's clock, not Chrome's `new Date()`.

The key challenge is testing relative times, things like "two hours ago," "last night," and "in 3 days." The crucial insight is that `Time.now` (wall-clock time) when `travel_to` isn't used *matches* Chrome's `new Date()`. Therefore, if I want to test relative dates against the browser's actual clock, I need to make the server clock and the browser clock match.

Here's my plan:

1.  **Timezone Override:** I'll use `page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: "America/New_York")` to set the browser's timezone. I'll test multiple timezones ("America/New\_York" and "Asia/Tokyo")

2.  **Relative Time Generation:** For relative time tests, I need to generate timestamps that are correctly interpreted relative to the browser's overridden timezone. Here's the trick: I'll pick a timezone where the current local time is in the afternoon (e.g., between 2 PM and 4 PM). I can leverage the fact that there is always a timezone on Earth where the local time falls in this range. The solution is to ensure that a timezone is selected such that when I do things like "two hours ago", it renders correctly and consistently.

For example, when generating "two hours ago," I'll ensure that the chosen timezone allows for this time to fall on the same calendar day. Similarly, I can compute the "last night" time as 23:30 of the previous day in that timezone. The general rule is: If I pick a timezone where the current hour is between 14 and 22, it will work. I'll have a lookup, which can be dynamically selected based on real wall-clock time. This ensures that:

*   "2 hours ago" will always be today.
*   "last night" (23:30 yesterday) is always less than 24 hours ago.
*   "5 days ago" is always "5 days ago".
*   "Sep 12" is consistent.
*   "Tomorrow" and "in 3 days" render correctly.

3.  **Cross-Timezone Verification:** I'll test the `Emulation.setTimezoneOverride` with *multiple* timezones. For instance, I'll visit the *same* card/comment with "America/New\_York" and then "Asia/Tokyo," ensuring the server renders the same *raw* timestamp (`2025-01-22T18:42:00Z`), but the rendered output correctly reflects the different timezones ("1:42 PM" in New York, "3:42 AM" the next day in Tokyo).

require "test_helper"

class TimeHelperTest < ActionView::TestCase
  def parse(html)
    Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(html)
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag emits raw UTC iso8601 timestamp without server clock text" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 17, 42, 0)

    Time.use_zone("America/New_York") do
      html = local_datetime_tag(timestamp, style: :relative)
      node = parse(html).at_css("time")

      assert_equal "2025-09-12T17:42:00Z", node["datetime"]
      assert_equal "local-time", node["data-controller"]
      assert_equal "relative", node["data-local-time-style-value"]
      assert_includes node["class"], "local-time-value"
      assert_equal "", node.text
      assert_nil node["title"]
    end
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag emits date-only iso8601 for Date objects" do
    date = Date.new(2025, 9, 12)
    html = local_datetime_tag(date, style: :daysdate)
    node = parse(html).at_css("time")

    assert_equal "2025-09-12", node["datetime"]
    assert_equal "daysdate", node["data-local-time-style-value"]
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag returns nil when datetime is nil" do
    assert_nil local_datetime_tag(nil)
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag merges custom classes and data attributes" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 17, 42, 0)
    html = local_datetime_tag(timestamp, style: :time, class: "custom-class", data: { controller: "tooltip", testid: "ts" })
    node = parse(html).at_css("time")

    assert_includes node["class"], "custom-class"

    assert_includes node["data-controller"], "tooltip"
    assert_equal "ts", node["data-testid"]

  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class LocalTimeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @card = cards(:layout)
  end

  test "renders comment and card timestamps in the viewer timezone" do
    timezone = afternoon_timezone
    set_browser_timezone(timezone)

    now_in_zone = Time.now.in_time_zone(timezone)
    two_hours_ago = now_in_zone - 2.hours
    last_night = now_in_zone.yesterday.change(hour: 23, min: 30)
    five_days_ago = now_in_zone - 5.days
    older_date = now_in_zone - 30.days

    @card.comments.delete_all
    c1 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment two hours ago", created_at: two_hours_ago)
    c2 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment last night", created_at: last_night)
    c3 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment five days ago", created_at: five_days_ago)
    c4 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment older", created_at: older_date)

    visit card_url(@card)

    expected_time = two_hours_ago.strftime("%-l:%M %p")
    expected_older = older_date.year == now_in_zone.year ? older_date.strftime("%b %-d") : older_date.strftime("%b %-d, %Y")

    within "##{dom_id(c1)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: expected_time
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c2)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /yesterday/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c3)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /5 days ago/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c4)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: expected_older
    end
  end

  test "renders auto-closing entropy notice as tomorrow and in N days" do
    timezone = afternoon_timezone
    set_browser_timezone(timezone)

    now_in_zone = Time.now.in_time_zone(timezone)
    period = @card.board.auto_postpone_period

    # Auto-closing overnight (tomorrow)
    overnight = now_in_zone.tomorrow.change(hour: 1, min: 0)
    @card.update_columns(last_active_at: overnight - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” tomorrow if there’s no activity."

    # Auto-closing in 3 days
    in_three_days = now_in_zone + 3.days
    @card.update_columns(last_active_at: in_three_days - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” in 3 days if there’s no activity."
  end

  test "same cached card renders different local times for viewers in different timezones" do
    comment = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Timezone test comment", created_at: Time.now.utc.change(min: 42))

    # Viewer 1 in America/New_York (UTC-5)
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit card_url(@card)
    ny_expected = comment.created_at.in_time_zone("America/New_York").strftime("%-l:%M %p")
    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      ny_text = find(".comment__permalink-title time").text
      assert_includes [ ny_expected, "Yesterday" ], ny_text
    end

    # Viewer 2 in Asia/Tokyo (UTC+9) hitting the same cached comment HTML
    set_browser_timezone("Asia/Tokyo")
    visit card_url(@card)
    tokyo_time = comment.created_at.in_time_zone("Asia/Tokyo")
    tokyo_now = Time.now.in_time_zone("Asia/Tokyo")
    tokyo_expected = if tokyo_time.to_date == tokyo_now.to_date
      tokyo_time.strftime("%-l:%M %p")
    else
      "Tomorrow"
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /#{Regexp.escape(tokyo_expected)}/i
    end
  end

  private
    include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

    def afternoon_timezone
      candidates = %w[
        UTC Europe/London America/New_York America/Chicago
        America/Los_Angeles Pacific/Honolulu Asia/Tokyo Australia/Sydney
      ]
      candidates.find { |tz| Time.now.in_time_zone(tz).hour.between?(14, 22) } || "UTC"
    end

    def set_browser_timezone(timezone_id)
      page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: timezone_id)
    end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class LocalTimeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @card = cards(:layout)
  end

  test "renders comment and card timestamps in the viewer timezone" do
    timezone = afternoon_timezone
    set_browser_timezone(timezone)

    now_in_zone = Time.now.in_time_zone(timezone)
    two_hours_ago = now_in_zone - 2.hours
    last_night = now_in_zone.yesterday.change(hour: 23, min: 30)
    five_days_ago = now_in_zone - 5.days
    older_date = now_in_zone - 30.days

    @card.comments.delete_all
    c1 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment two hours ago", created_at: two_hours_ago)
    c2 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment last night", created_at: last_night)
    c3 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment five days ago", created_at: five_days_ago)
    c4 = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Comment older", created_at: older_date)

    visit card_url(@card)

    expected_time = two_hours_ago.strftime("%-l:%M %p")
    expected_older = older_date.year == now_in_zone.year ? older_date.strftime("%b %-d") : older_date.strftime("%b %-d, %Y")

    within "##{dom_id(c1)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: expected_time
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c2)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /yesterday/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c3)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /5 days ago/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(c4)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: expected_older
    end
  end

  test "renders auto-closing entropy notice and bubble in the viewer timezone" do
    timezone = afternoon_timezone
    set_browser_timezone(timezone)

    now_in_zone = Time.now.in_time_zone(timezone)
    period = @card.board.auto_postpone_period

    # Auto-closing overnight (tomorrow)
    overnight = now_in_zone.tomorrow.change(hour: 1, min: 0)
    @card.update_columns(last_active_at: overnight - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” tomorrow if there’s no activity."
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :bubble)} .bubble__number", text: "1"

    # Auto-closing in 3 days
    in_three_days = now_in_zone + 3.days
    @card.update_columns(last_active_at: in_three_days - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” in 3 days if there’s no activity."
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :bubble)} .bubble__number", text: "3"
  end

  test "renders closed card stamp and completion notice in the viewer timezone" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    closed_time = Time.utc(2025, 9, 13, 2, 0, 0) # Sep 12, 2025 10:00 PM EDT in America/New_York
    @card.close(user: users(:david))
    @card.closure.update_columns(created_at: closed_time)
    @card.touch

    visit card_url(@card)

    assert_selector ".card__closed-date time", text: /Sep 12, 2025/i
    assert_selector ".card-perma__closure-message", text: /Completed by David on Sep 12, 2025\./
  end

  test "renders different local times for viewers in different timezones from the same cached HTML" do
    comment = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:david), body: "Timezone test comment", created_at: 1.hour.ago)

    # Viewer 1 in America/New_York
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit card_url(@card)
    ny_time = comment.created_at.in_time_zone("America/New_York")
    ny_now = Time.now.in_time_zone("America/New_York")
    ny_expected = ny_time.to_date == ny_now.to_date ? ny_time.strftime("%-l:%M %p") : "Yesterday"

    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /#{Regexp.escape(ny_expected)}/i
    end
    ny_rendered = find("##{dom_id(comment)} .comment__permalink-title time").text

    # Viewer 2 in Asia/Tokyo
    set_browser_timezone("Asia/Tokyo")
    visit card_url(@card)
    tokyo_time = comment.created_at.in_time_zone("Asia/Tokyo")
    tokyo_now = Time.now.in_time_zone("Asia/Tokyo")
    tokyo_expected = tokyo_time.to_date == tokyo_now.to_date ? tokyo_time.strftime("%-l:%M %p") : "Yesterday"

    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      assert_selector ".comment__permalink-title time", text: /#{Regexp.escape(tokyo_expected)}/i
    end
    tokyo_rendered = find("##{dom_id(comment)} .comment__permalink-title time").text

    assert_not_equal ny_rendered, tokyo_rendered
  end

  test "keeps timestamps rendered after a Turbo morph refresh" do
    timezone = afternoon_timezone
    set_browser_timezone(timezone)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :meta)} .card__meta-text--added time", text: /\S+/
    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all

    @card.update!(title: "Morphed card title")
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Morphed card title", wait: 5
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :meta)} .card__meta-text--added time", text: /\S+/
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :meta)} .card__meta-text--updated time", text: /\S+/
  end

  test "renders activity timeline timestamps in browser" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit root_url

    assert_selector ".events__column-header time", text: Time.now.in_time_zone("America/New_York").strftime("%A, %B %-d").upcase
  end

  private
    def afternoon_timezone
      candidates = %w[
        UTC Europe/London America/New_York America/Chicago
        America/Los_Angeles Pacific/Honolulu Asia/Tokyo Australia/Sydney
      ]
      candidates.find { |tz| Time.now.in_time_zone(tz).hour.between?(14, 22) } || "UTC"
    end

    def set_browser_timezone(timezone_id)
      page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: timezone_id)
    end
end
EOF

Okay, here's my take on those thoughts, tailored for an expert audience:

**Local Time Testing & Caching Strategy**

Excellent! The `local_time_test.rb` system tests are all green. That's a good sign, especially the Turbo morph refresh - a tricky area. Now, the next step is crucial: verifying the timezone independence of our cached HTML.

I need to nail down the integration tests for `local_time_caching_test.rb`. The objective is clear. I want complete assurance that when we cache cards, comments, notifications, or anything else involving time, the resulting HTML *must* be agnostic to the user's timezone. This means the cached output should *only* include raw UTC ISO8601 `<time>` tags. No server-side rendering of date/time strings, no localized formats – just the standardized, unambiguous UTC representation.

We have to ensure our caching strategy completely avoids timezone-related rendering differences and the complexities that arise from them. This test will be pivotal in maintaining consistent behavior across all timezones and server configurations.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > test/integration/local_time_caching_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class LocalTimeCachingTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include CachingTestHelper

  setup do
    @card = cards(:layout)
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Cached comment", created_at: Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 17, 42, 0))
  end

  test "cached card and comment HTML is identical across viewer timezones and contains raw UTC timestamps" do
    with_actionview_partial_caching do
      sign_in_as :kevin
      cookies[:timezone] = "America/New_York"
      get card_path(@card)
      assert_response :success
      ny_body = response.body

      sign_in_as :david
      cookies[:timezone] = "Asia/Tokyo"
      get card_path(@card)
      assert_response :success
      tokyo_body = response.body

      assert_select Nokogiri::HTML(ny_body), "time[datetime='2025-09-12T17:42:00Z']", count: 1
      assert_select Nokogiri::HTML(tokyo_body), "time[datetime='2025-09-12T17:42:00Z']", count: 1

      # Neither response contains server-rendered clock text for the comment
      assert_no_match(/1:42 PM|12:42 PM|2:42 AM|ago/, Nokogiri::HTML(ny_body).at_css("##{ActionView::RecordIdentifier.dom_id(@comment)} .comment__permalink-title").text)
      assert_no_match(/1:42 PM|12:42 PM|2:42 AM|ago/, Nokogiri::HTML(tokyo_body).at_css("##{ActionView::RecordIdentifier.dom_id(@comment)} .comment__permalink-title").text)
      assert_no_match(/ago/, Nokogiri::HTML(ny_body).at_css("##{ActionView::RecordIdentifier.dom_id(@card, :meta)}").text)
    end
  end

  test "public card HTML does not leak viewer timezone" do
    boards(:writebook).publish

    cookies[:timezone] = "America/New_York"
    get public_board_card_path(boards(:writebook).publication.key, cards(:logo))
    assert_response :success

    assert_no_match(/America\/New_York/, response.body)
    assert_select "meta[name='timezone']", count: 0
    assert_select "time[data-controller='local-time'][datetime]"
  end
end
EOF

bin/rails test test/integration/local_time_caching_test.rb
